rows.review: Coset-Helly expands arbitrary standard-parabolic cosets into maximal ones. Residue identification uses a common representative; residual generation applies only to residues of rank at least two. These are needed background forms, not blanket recovery of every variant of external background theorems.

The common induction retains A_S in empty support and requires residual generation. Both elementary C2^3 examples in the application are actual coset geometries under the source convention; one connected geometry has nontrivial Borel, and one disconnected geometry still satisfies generated-support intersections.
Old and new panel counts are indices over the actual Borel, obtained from common parabolic intersections; no faithfulness shortcut is used.

Coordinate projection gives a coset bijection preserving incidence, and intersection formulas follow componentwise. Full-product flags can be realized coordinatewise. In finite type, chamber indices give geometry finiteness independently of faithfulness of the acting group.

Restricted and unrestricted products give the same disjoint-union join because one/two nonidentity coordinates suffice for elements/incidence. Whole flags can require infinitely many coordinate moves; residue connectivity uses two nonempty factors or the one remaining factor. Arbitrary coordinate choices retain the usual axiom of choice.

An infinite family of one-chamber factors is a literal counterexample to the unrestricted word never. The exact obstruction requires infinitely many factors permitting distinct same-type flags; firm nonempty factors meet that condition.

Read the complete previously reviewed proof and current coordinates. B acts on the indexed type set and permutes actual maximal parabolics; IPO gives E(J), not an unjustified generated-support formula. Coset projection followed by normalization reduces flag realization to the common A Helly statement.

All three residue cases are supplied: no missing orbit type, no missing old type, and mixed. The mixed case contains B_J and conjugates the other A-parabolic; intersection of its translated index sets is E(J), so the parabolic-generation lemma applies.

Index lower bounds follow from the retained Borel and a single selected point. For a general twist, fixed representatives give sufficient thinness; the wreath coordinate product gives the exact if-and-only-if condition.

The full finite-type flag-transitive theorem permits unfaithful inputs and nontrivial Borel; geometry finiteness is equivalent to both input geometries being finite, not to finite acting groups. Firmness and connectivity have explicit hypotheses.

Trivial Borels give regular chamber action. Chamber propagation shows this is the full type-preserving automorphism group. Quotient passage uses saturated intersections C_E containing H, with H normal and invisible on the quotient geometry; it does not substitute arbitrary images of generated supports.

Verified arm permutations, orbits, both displayed edge lists and all standard subgroups via the common construction. Changing the representative changes G7 from S4 times C2 to S3 times D8; abelianizations 4 and 8 distinguish them. The path model has labels 3,4,3,4. Classical Coxeter parabolic embedding remains retained.

The explicit vertex/face-to-cube-vertex bijection, incident-pair edges and tetrahedron-edge faces preserve every incidence. This identifies the cube independently of merely having group order 48. Dual ordering accounts for the two printed string types.

For each orbit and each original type, representatives may differ. The action on (j,omega) has precisely the stated orbit-intersection condition. All coordinate parabolics in Proposition 2 retain that dependence.

G_i has factor A_Ei(omega), unrestricted on the selected support in the coherent case and Borel outside. G_L has A_j inside the orbit and A outside. This is the complement direction obtained from the defining intersections; the literal source reverses it and omits Borels.

For thin inputs each new panel index is 2 to the size of the Borel orbit. Thus thinness is equivalent to singleton selected orbits. The rank-one C2 and (S3,C3) construction gives K2,8 in order48. Factoring B by its kernel cannot preserve a coordinate action on which that kernel acts nontrivially.

The full module theorem is arbitrary-rank, with nested prefix spans allowing dependencies; Young blocks are fixed individually. The cocycle automorphism fixes V and sends ordinary adjacent swaps to exactly the q_i. The third odd-rank group may move to another embedded complement, which is explicitly allowed.

The diagram adapter identifies actual marked permutations, so graph16 odd rank follows from the ordinary seed by an automorphism. This closes the source-recorded unverified IP case; it is not a claim of historical priority or of the full external classification. Source classification range r>=7 and algebraic range r>=2 remain distinct.
The application includes the exact D16 automorphism computation and commuting-lift contradiction, so it does not assume an automatic action of Out(A). It specifies an actual reversal automorphism.

A self-duality followed by an automorphism fixes the base chamber as a set. Its square fixes types and that chamber, hence is identity; conjugation gives the required nontrivial involutory group automorphism.

Doubled-label exactness follows from projection to C2 and (a_i t)^2=a_i a_reverse(i). For n>=6 t has degree at least3. For n4/5 the stated sufficient p0>2 condition produces a triangle. All-digon rank4 is a valid regular abstract polytope and its reversal extension cannot have any triple of involutions with all pairs noncommuting.

Checked representatives 0,1 for n3; 0,2 for n4; 0,2,3 for n5. Their stated orderings are strings, including permitted labels2. The source n4 pair0,3 repeats a single orbit. For the nonlinear n5 selection the diagram is a triangle with possible pendant edge, not the stated square.

For outer tau the natural conjugation map has kernel Z(A) times1: an outside kernel element would make tau inner. The rank3 all-digon example has order16 but Aut(C2^3) has order168, excluding even an abstract embedding. This does not affect centerless sporadic applications.

All ten literal affirmative cases are paid by the nine-case and HN packets. Verified each saved program, group-identification route, all marking intersections and actual product-set flag tests. HN generation uses outer c, saved prime-order words and the retained complete thirteen-maximal list. O Nan uses a valid direct construction despite the impossible source outer-duality route.
Fi22 and Fi24prime are outside this reviewed affirmative contract; no statement about any separate new candidate is accepted here.

Cosets identify configurations and one unspecified lamp. A path changes finitely many coordinates and every finite difference can be toggled, so components are exactly D/D_fin. The corrected squared presentation has unique lamp normal forms. Literal source physical20 omits the square and presents C2 times Z; fresh large raster confirms the omission.

Classical nonfinite-presentability of the restricted lamplighter remains a retained ancillary fact, not an inference about the literal finitely presentable C2 times Z and not a premise for the component argument.
